title: Members CLI for the waitlist and enablement
description:
**Phase 3 of 7.** Bootstrap path for enablement. 5744ef cannot seed the first organization, and 7b4616 cannot close the door, without this CLI.

- **Blocked by:** b574a6
- **Runs in parallel with:** every other phase-3 task
- **Unblocks:** 5744ef, then 7b4616

---
python -m chatticus.members with list --status pending, enable, suspend, and role. This is the admin surface for v1; there is no admin UI. Organization records are data, not infrastructure, so writing them from a CLI does not violate the CDK-only rule for AWS resources.

**Done when:** an operator can list pending organizations and enable one against development.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Heads-up before this surfaces a semantic that is not settled yet.**

`enable_organization` in #130 writes `ENABLED` from any prior state, so it approves a pending organization and reinstates a suspended one through the same call. A review note on b574a6 asks for those to be separated.

For this CLI: do not expose a single `members enable` that can do both. An operator clearing a waitlist backlog should not be able to silently reinstate an organization that somebody suspended for cause. Either wait for b574a6 to split the operation, or have the CLI refuse to enable an organization whose status is `SUSPENDED` and point at an explicit reinstate command.

Everything else on this card stands, and it is the right thing to be working: 41d08d unblocks 5744ef, which 7b4616 cannot be called done without.

comments.author: agent@example.com
comments.text:
**Architect review taken.**

#132 (`python -m chatticus.members`) does not expose a combined enable/reinstate. `members enable` loads the org, prints tenant/name/status/owner, then refuses unless status is pending (`OrganizationStatusTransitionError`). Suspended organizations cannot be enabled through this CLI.

The kernel in the same PR matches: `enable_organization` accepts only PENDING; `suspend_organization` accepts only ENABLED. There is still no named `reinstate_organization` — that stays a follow-up on the control plane, not this bootstrap CLI. Waitlist enablement does not silently unsuspend.

Holding merge for CI. Card stays open until an operator can list pending and enable against the development messaging table.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Reviewed #132. The enable-versus-reinstate note was answered better than it was asked, and the answer left a door with no handle.**

Guards at both layers, not just the kernel one I suggested: `_cmd_enable` refuses anything that is not `PENDING`, `_cmd_suspend` refuses anything that is not `ENABLED`, and `org_records` enforces the same transitions underneath, with pytest asserting both raises. The CLI prints an organization summary before acting and requires `--yes`. For an operation that provisions recurring cost, making the operator look at what they are about to enable is the right shape.

**The consequence: `SUSPENDED` is now terminal.** Subcommands are `list`, `show`, `enable`, `suspend`. `enable` refuses a suspended organization, and no reinstate exists, so nothing can move an organization out of `SUSPENDED` through any interface. Separating the two acts was right; the separation is only half-built until the second act exists.

Not a blocker for this card, whose done-when is listing pending organizations and enabling one, and that works. But the first person to suspend an organization discovers the trap, and they discover it at the moment they most want it undone. Carded separately.

CI was still running when I looked, so this is a review note rather than a merge signal.
